title: USB VIP example tb_usb_svt_uvm_intermediate_sys -- PIPE3/PIPE4 SuperSpeed, user covergroup on VIP coverage callback, uvm_in_order_comparator scoreboard, hand-tuned LTSSM timers
summary:
tb_usb_svt_uvm_intermediate_sys is the best example for the COVERAGE aspect (only one with a hand-written covergroup extending the VIP's own built-in coverage callback) and for PIPE3/PIPE4 SuperSpeed interface + LTSSM timer tuning.

COVERAGE: env/usb_intermediate_protocol_ss_host_coverage_callbacks.sv extends svt_usb_protocol_monitor_ss_host_def_cov_callback (a VIP-provided default coverage callback base). Defines `covergroup user_defined_transfer_cover_group` with coverpoints on transfer_type (bins control/bulk_in/bulk_out, option.weight=0) and transfer_length (bins min_length=[0:8]/mid_length=[9:512]/max_length=[513:5000], option.weight=0), plus a cross transfer_type_X_transfer_length with `ignore_bins control_max_length = binsof(transfer_type.control) && binsof(transfer_length.max_length)` (pruned because a CONTROL transfer can never be max_length given the payload_intended_byte_count_control_out<=512 constraint from cust_svt_usb_transfer). The 3-step extension pattern: override transfer_ended() to capture transfer_length=xfer.payload_byte_count() (a derived field the built-in class doesn't expose to the covergroup), override sample_cov() to call `super.sample_cov(coverage_type)` FIRST (let the VIP sample its own built-in bins) THEN `user_defined_transfer_cover_group.sample()`. Registered via `uvm_callbacks#(svt_usb_protocol_monitor)::add(host_agent.prot_mon, cb_for_host_cov)` in usb_intermediate_pipe4_env::build_phase -- attaches to .prot_mon (the PROTOCOL MONITOR), a THIRD distinct callback attach point confirmed across examples: .prot for driver-side callbacks (transfer_observed_port, objection mgmt), .prot_mon for monitor/coverage callbacks, .link/.downstream_agent[i].link for link-layer callbacks (see the basic_router_sys record). Coverage sampling only actually fires if build_phase also sets `cfg.host_cfg.enable_prot_cov=1; cfg.host_cfg.enable_link_cov=1;` -- these config fields gate whether VIP-internal coverage (and thus this callback) runs at all.

ENVIRONMENT/INTERFACE: usb_intermediate_pipe4_env.sv adds virtual svt_usb_if usb_ss_phy_if AND usb_ss_mac_if (separate PHY-side and MAC-side handles -- PIPE-interface testbenches split the SS interface into two virtual interface handles because PIPE is a MAC<->PHY chip-to-chip bus, unlike serial which is one bidirectional differential pair), a `bit disable_scoreboard` config knob letting a test opt OUT of scoreboard construction entirely, and the SAME remote_cfg-clone-as-PHY pattern as basic_router_sys but gated specifically on `usb_ss_signal_interface==PIPE4_IF||PIPE3_IF` (hub_basic_env's gate additionally includes UTMI_IF) -- i.e. remote_cfg cloning is required whenever EITHER side of a link is a MAC-side PIPE/UTMI interface, regardless of topology complexity. connect_phase connects the scoreboard DIRECTLY to the VIP's own analysis port (`host_agent.prot.transfer_observed_port.connect(usb_scoreboard.host_export)`) -- the simpler single-hop alternative to basic_router_sys's event-repolling indirection, sufficient whenever only transfer-level (not transaction/packet-level) comparison across a single host/device pair is needed.

SCOREBOARD: usb_uvm_scoreboard.sv is the SIMPLEST of 3 distinct scoreboard architectures in the example set (vs basic_router_sys's hand-rolled dual-queue+event search-based scoreboards). It delegates entirely to UVM's built-in uvm_in_order_comparator#(svt_usb_transfer, usb_transfer_comp#(svt_usb_transfer), uvm_class_converter#(svt_usb_transfer)), with a static usb_transfer_comp::comp(a,b) wrapper using uvm_comparer.physical=1/.abstract=0 (RELEVANT policy). host_export/device_export connect to comparator.before_export/after_export; report_phase prints comparator.m_matches/m_mismatches and declares TEST FAIL/PASS. This assumes host and device transfers arrive in the SAME relative order on both sides (no endpoint/address re-matching search) -- correct ONLY for simple single-host/single-device comparison; multi-device hub scenarios need the hand-rolled search-based approach instead (cross-reference: basic_router_sys record).

TEST/CONFIGURATION: usb_ess_pipe4_base_test.sv sets cfg.host_cfg.usb_ss_signal_interface=PIPE4_IF; cfg.dev_cfg.usb_ss_signal_interface=USB_SS_TLM (host=MAC/PIPE side, device=abstract TLM side) then explicitly overrides ~40 individual LTSSM timer/count fields (receiver_detect_time, rx_detect_quiet_timeout, p2_to_p0_transition_time, tx_lfps_duty_cycle, polling_lfps_burst_time, polling_lfps_sent_count, polling_active_received_ts_count, polling_configuration_{received,sent}_ts2_count, polling_idle_{received,sent}_idle_count, ltssm_skip_polling_rxeq, polling_rxeq_tseq_count) with HOST and DEVICE INTENTIONALLY set to DIFFERENT values for the same parameter (comment: 'intentionally programmed to different values to demonstrate VIPs usage that suits DUTs timers') -- the reference pattern for modeling a real DUT's asymmetric PHY timing rather than assuming symmetric host/device VIP timing. Also sets usb_ss_automatic_lmp_disable=1 on both sides so the test can exit right after U0 without auto-exchanged LMPs. main_phase starts usb_device_response_sequence on env.dev_agent.xfer_response_sequencer (a separate RESPONSE sequencer distinct from xfer_sequencer) then blocks on shared_status.ltssm_state==U0 AND shared_status.lmp_generation_completed_status==NORMALLY.

SEQUENCE: usb_ltssm_sequence.sv (extends uvm_sequence#(svt_usb_link_service), a THIRD distinct sequence-item type beyond svt_usb_transfer and svt_usb_protocol_service) sends a single svt_usb_link_service item with service_type=LINK_SS_PORT_COMMAND, link_ss_command_type=USB_SS_POWER_ON_RESET, prereq_ltssm_state=svt_usb_types::SS_DISABLED -- the VIP only executes the command once LTSSM reaches/is-at that prerequisite state, letting sequences fire early and self-gate on protocol state. Per-USB3-spec comment: device-side SS.Disabled->Rx.Detect does NOT require an explicit command (only host/downstream-facing ports do) -- host and device LTSSM entry are asymmetric from the very first transition.
